title: Geometric points of algebraic spaces: topos points, conservativity and inverse image
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $T$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], using the universes and small-site convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. A geometric point $\bar t$ is a map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. A pointed etale neighbourhood is an etale scheme $U\to T$ together with a lift $\bar t\to U$; arrows are maps over $T$ respecting the lifts. For a sheaf of sets $F$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, define $F_{\bar t}$ as the colimit of $F(U)$ over the opposite of this neighbourhood category. This functor is the inverse image of a point $p_{\bar t}:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{et}})$, where a point means an adjunction $p^{-1}\dashv p_*$ with $p^{-1}$ preserving finite limits [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism, with the ring structures omitted]. A map of sheaves of sets on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ is injective, respectively surjective, if and only if its maps on all geometric stalks are injective, respectively surjective. In particular these stalks jointly detect isomorphisms. For every morphism $h:T\to W$ of algebraic spaces over $S$, the geometric morphism on small etale topoi sends $p_{\bar t}$ to $p_{h\bar t}$: there are canonical natural identifications $(h^{-1}F)_{\bar t}\cong F_{h\bar t}$ for every sheaf $F$ on $W_{\mathrm{et}}$, compatible with the maps on stalk rings and with algebraic operations carried by sheaves.

source.place: Tags 04K0 (lemma-stalk-gives-point), 04K2(4) (lemma-stalk-pullback), and 04K5 (theorem-exactness-stalks). Use geometric points of T, as in the first sentence of 04K5 and its proof; the final sentence there prints S for X.

proof.text: Fix $\bar t$. Put $L(U)=\operatorname{Hom}_T(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,U)$ and, for a set $A$, define $P_A(U)=\operatorname{Map}(L(U),A)$, with restriction by precomposition. This is a sheaf. Indeed a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ is a jointly surjective etale family of schemes by the definition of the small site. Every $l\in L(U)$ lifts to some $l_i\in L(U_i)$ by the cited geometric-point lifting lemma, applied to the scheme $U$ and the geometric point $l$ with the original algebraically closed field $\Omega$. Given matching functions $a_i:L(U_i)\to A$, set $a(l)=a_i(l_i)$. Two lifts $l_i,l_j$ of $l$ give a unique lift to $U_i\times_U U_j$ by the scheme fibre-product universal property; the matching condition therefore makes $a(l)$ independent of both choices. This gives the unique glued function, also when $L(U)$ is empty. Functoriality in $A$ is postcomposition, so $A\mapsto P_A$ is a functor to sheaves. All sets and neighbourhood colimits lie in the fixed universe.

source.place: Tag 00Y8, lemma-point-pushforward-sheaf (1), explicit matching-family proof; lifting input: etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03PR, lemma-geometric-lift-to-cover

proof.text: There is a natural adjunction $F\mapsto F_{\bar t}\dashv(A\mapsto P_A)$. Explicitly a function $b:F_{\bar t}\to A$ gives the sheaf map $\alpha_U(s)(l)=b([U,l,s])$. Conversely a sheaf map $\alpha:F\to P_A$ gives $b([U,l,s])=\alpha_U(s)(l)$. The latter respects every colimit relation because naturality says $\alpha_V(F(f)s)(l)=\alpha_U(s)(f l)$ for $f:V\to U$; the two recipes are inverse and natural in $F,A$. The colimit here is exactly the opposite-neighbourhood colimit in the statement. The cited conservative-stalk node states that this same functor preserves finite limits. Taking $p_{\bar t}^{-1}F=F_{\bar t}$ and $(p_{\bar t})_*A=P_A$ therefore gives a point of the topos in the stated sense of an adjunction with left exact left adjoint.

source.place: Tags 00Y8, lemma-point-pushforward-sheaf (2), and 00YA, lemma-point-site-topos (1); spaces-properties.tex Tag 04K0, lemma-stalk-gives-point, identifies this stalk

proof.text: Apply the cited conservative-stalk node with $X=T$. Its colimit uses the same pointed etale scheme neighbourhoods, and it states precisely the equivalences between monomorphisms, epimorphisms and isomorphisms of sheaves and injective, surjective and bijective maps on all geometric stalks. Thus it gives the claimed injectivity and surjectivity criteria (surjectivity of sheaves means local surjectivity, or epimorphism), and joint detection of isomorphisms. In particular no assertion of surjectivity on sections of every object is used. For $T=\varnothing$ its stated empty-space clause gives the same conclusions despite the empty family of geometric points.

source.place: Tag 04K5, theorem-exactness-stalks, first assertion and proof

proof.text: For $h:T\to W$, use the canonical small-etale geometric morphism of the enlarged ringed-site model. Apply the cited chart-comparison node to get $c_F:(h^{-1}F)_{\bar t}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{h\bar t}$ naturally in $F$. That node is phrased over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, so first apply [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] to $S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$: by its clause (1) $j_!T$ and $j_!W$ are algebraic spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and $j_!h$ is a morphism of them, and by its clause (3) the small etale sites of $T$ and $j_!T$ (and of $W$ and $j_!W$) are identified with their coverings and structure sheaves, carrying $V\mapsto V\times_WT$ to the base-change functor of $j_!h$. Geometric points correspond, since any scheme over $T$ acquires its unique compatible $S$-structure by composition. Hence the topos morphism and ring map of the chart-comparison node for $j_!h$ are those for the present $h$, and so is its stalk comparison. This identifies inverse images of the two points; their right adjoints are then canonically identified by the same adjunction bijections. For algebraic compatibility, naturality with the projections from $F^n$ gives $c_{F^n}=c_F^n$ under the finite-product identifications, and the terminal-object case gives compatibility with constants. Naturality with each operation $F^n\to F$ now says $c_F$ preserves it; the same argument with products of different sheaves covers scalar actions. Finally the structural ring map $h^{-1}\mathcal O_W\to\mathcal O_T$ from the ringed-site model gives on stalks the composite $\mathcal O_{W,h\bar t}\xrightarrow{c_{\mathcal O_W}^{-1}}(h^{-1}\mathcal O_W)_{\bar t}\to\mathcal O_{T,\bar t}$. This is the canonical stalk-ring map, with its chartwise description supplied by the chart-comparison node. Thus the point comparison respects ring maps and the algebraic operations as asserted.
